company.tagline: Single-origin Tellicherry pepper, cleaned and graded in Kerala, shipped from the Malabar coast under our own mark.
company.one_liner: A Kerala pepper house that owns the grade, the testing, and the story — instead of exporting anonymous bulk to whoever bids last.
company.origin_hub: Western Ghats growing belt within ~200 km of Kochi: Idukki, Pathanamthitta, Wayanad, Kasaragod

wedge.statement: India grows the world's most storied pepper and exports very little of it. The 2024/25 crop fell to a record-low ~48,000 t while domestic consumption ran ~81,000 t — so India net-imported. Buyers who want genuine Indian-origin pepper pay a premium for it, and they cannot tell where any given bag came from.
wedge.insight: The scarce input is not pepper — it is verified Indian provenance at lot level. Our moat is the paper trail plus the grading, not the commodity.
wedge.strategy: Buy small, cherry-pick the top-grade fraction of Kerala lots, steam-treat and test each lot to destination spec, then sell retail-ready packs and B2B micro-lots under our own mark. Never trade volume for its own sake.

channel_tiers.buyer: Farmer sells to a village aggregator; ungraded, no testing
channel_tiers.source: Kochi terminal indicative black pepper price, Jun 2025, Rs 670-685/kg; farm-gate discounts to terminal of roughly 8-10% implied

channel_tiers.buyer: Cleans, grades, bulks in 25 kg bags, sells FOB on spot
channel_tiers.source: FOB range USD 3.45-8.50/kg by grade; USD 4.50-6.00 for MG-1 whole. INR 760/kg ≈ USD 8.6/kg at 88.5 INR/USD, above published FOB because this line includes margin of the processor

channel_tiers.buyer: Importer into EU/US pays CIF; duty is 0% on whole pepper into both
channel_tiers.source: FOB plus freight and insurance: ~USD 4,650 per container Nhava Sheva-Antwerp ÷ ~19 t net for a 20ft of bagged spice ≈ USD 0.24/kg freight. Retail-grade landed expectation from buyer-side quotes

channel_tiers.buyer: Buyer pays shelf price for 100 g - 1 kg branded packs
channel_tiers.source: Observed 2025-26 retail: EUR 36.93/kg (FR, 1 kg), GBP 27.95/kg (UK, 1 kg), USD 33.19/lb = USD 73/kg (US, 1 lb bag), EUR 50/kg (DE, 50 g). INR 2,400/kg = USD 27.1/kg = GBP ~21/kg, i.e. below the cheapest observed single-kilo retail price

risks.risk: Ethylene oxide contamination in incoming lots
risks.why: EtO is banned for food use in the EU; the EU measures EtO plus 2-chloroethanol at a default limit around 0.02-0.1 mg/kg. A positive result destroys the shipment.
risks.control: Contract clause with every supplier: no EtO fumigation. Test every lot before it leaves India. Steam treatment only. Reject-on-positive with cost recovery.

risks.risk: Aflatoxin and ochratoxin A above EU limit
risks.why: EU limits for pepper: aflatoxin B1 5.0 ug/kg, total aflatoxins 10.0 ug/kg, ochratoxin A 15 ug/kg.
risks.control: Moisture spec max 12% at intake, covered drying, per-lot mycotoxin panel, reject lots from suppliers with two failures in a season.

risks.why: EU microbiological criteria require absence in 25 g; RASFF flags spices routinely.
risks.control: Validated steam treatment, post-treatment re-test, sealed liners, no re-bagging in open air.

risks.risk: Origin fraud — cheaper foreign pepper re-bagged as Indian
risks.why: This is the exact problem the company exists to solve, and the market's default behaviour.
risks.control: Lot-level chain of custody, named grower clusters, isotope and trace-element screening on a sampling basis, published lot numbers.

risks.why: The 2024/25 crop fell to ~48,000 t; India net-imported. Prices at Kochi moved through Rs 670-685/kg in mid-2025.
risks.control: Forward contracts with two grower clusters, inventory never above 90 days, price-adjust B2B quotes every 30 days, no fixed-price retail commitments longer than 6 months.

risks.why: Specialty food CAC is easy to overspend on in the first year.
risks.control: Hard 90-day cut rule on any channel above USD 18 CAC; shift budget to B2B where repeat is contractual.

risks.why: One bad monsoon in one district can remove a grade entirely.
risks.control: Two sourcing districts minimum, plus a standing second source for MG-1 outside the premium line.

india_export_stack.why: Mandatory for any food business incl. export

india_export_stack.item: CRES (Certificate of Registration as Exporter of Spices)
india_export_stack.why: No scheduled spice may be exported without it; treated as RCMC under FTP 2023
Needed for preferential claims and buyer files
Refund of embedded taxes on exports; file per shipping bill

eu.vat_note: Destination VAT applies on customs value plus duty
limits: Aflatoxin B1 max 5.0 ug/kg; total aflatoxins max 10.0 ug/kg (Reg (EU) 2023/915)
Ochratoxin A max 15 ug/kg for pepper
Ethylene oxide and 2-chloroethanol: measured as sum, at or near the limit of quantification — treat as zero tolerance
Lead max 0.6 mg/kg for fruit spices
eu.border_note: Pepper of heading 0904 from India is subject to a pesticide-residue check frequency at EU border control posts; confirm current Annex I frequency before each campaign

requirements: FDA registration and prior notice for every shipment
Foreign Supplier Verification Program (FSVP) obligations sit on the US importer — we supply the hazard analysis and verification records to make them workable
No US tolerance exists for EtO residues on spices; a detectable residue is a serious problem, not a threshold to negotiate

uk.note: UK-EU and UK-India arrangements change; confirm origin rules before claiming preference

quality_specs.packaging: Food-grade liner inside multi-wall paper or kraft with valve; nitrogen flush optional

lot_gate: Supplier declaration of no EtO fumigation, signed

Full panel: mycotoxins, microbiology, heavy metals, pesticide multi-residue, EtO
Grade verification by sieve and density
Only then does the lot receive a KL-YYYY-NNN lot number and enter sellable stock

brand_voice.profile_source: Derived from the ECC brand-voice skill's extraction dimensions, applied to a food-origin company rather than a software company.
do: Name the grade, the lot, and the test result
Use numbers where a number exists
Say what we reject and why, not just what we accept
dont: Never use 'exotic', 'authentic', 'premium quality', 'hand-picked by farmers' without a grade or a test behind it
brand_voice.sample_sentence: Lot KL-2026-014. TGSEB grade, 5.2 mm sieve, 6.1% piperine, EtO not detected, Salmonella absent in 25 g. That is the whole pitch.
